intent: Close the file-length cap's blind spot for extensionless scripts, and split the one file that had been hiding in it: boot_recovery/boot-repair at 756 lines.
scope: meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh - is_source_file() now also matches extensionless files with a shebang
One real bug fixed: an unquoted expansion that was invisible while the file escaped linting
changes: is_source_file() previously required a dot in the filename, so every extensionless executable escaped the cap. It now reads the first two bytes and accepts a shebang, which catches boot-repair while still skipping data files like i3/config.
Split boot-repair along its own section markers into four sourced libraries: discovery (paths, kernel, ESP, mount state), repair_fs, repair_kernel, and modes.

The end-of-run report block stays INLINE deliberately. It is top-level code with exit calls, not function definitions; sourcing it changed control flow and 30 of 42 tests failed. The lib headers record that.
Quoted $ESP_MOUNTPOINT in clean_shadow_files. shellcheck could not see the readonly declaration once the function moved to a library, which exposed a genuine SC2086 that the monolith had been hiding.

verification.evidence: 42 passed, 0 failed - the same count as before the split. These run the real script against throwaway fixture root trees, so they exercise the sourcing chain end to end.

31 of 32 functions byte-identical. The single difference is clean_shadow_files, which is the intended quoting fix and nothing else - the tool names the function, so the change is auditable rather than assumed.

verification.command: shellcheck on the entry script and all four libs
verification.evidence: Clean at every severity, with no suppression added.

Immediately after widening the predicate: '756 linux_configuration/boot_recovery/boot-repair (+506)'. After the split: 'all checked files are within 250 lines'. The other extensionless scripts (.githooks/pre-commit 119, dwm/bin/* 79/41/30) were already under.

risks: boot-repair is UEFI/ESP tooling and the vmbox guest is BIOS/GRUB, so a sandbox pass would be actively misleading here - per the vmbox skill's own warning. The fixture suite is the real evidence, and it runs the script against synthetic root trees rather than the live boot path.
live_test.sh needs root and was not run; it also required root before this change.
The report block remaining inline means boot-repair cannot go much below 218 lines without restructuring its control flow, which is not worth the risk on this file.
rollback: git revert restores the monolith and the narrower predicate together.
